text_blocks.snippet: With effective antiretroviral therapy (ART), people with HIV can achieve a life expectancy comparable to that of HIV-negative individuals, particularly when treatment is started early and viral suppression is achieved. However, co-morbidities can still impact the overall health and potentially reduce the number of years lived in good health.
snippet_highlighted_words: With effective antiretroviral therapy (ART), people with HIV can achieve a life expectancy comparable to that of HIV-negative individuals

list.title: Early initiation of ART:
list.snippet: Starting ART soon after HIV diagnosis and maintaining viral suppression significantly improves life expectancy.

list.title: CD4 count:
list.snippet: Higher CD4 cell counts at the start of ART and sustained levels are associated with longer life expectancies, according to some research.

list.title: Viral load:
list.snippet: Achieving undetectable viral load through ART is crucial for long-term health and life expectancy.

list.title: Co-morbidities:
list.snippet: Conditions like hepatitis B, hepatitis C, drug or alcohol abuse, and smoking can negatively impact life expectancy, according to a study.

list.title: Access to quality care:
list.snippet: Consistent access to high-quality healthcare, including ART and management of co-morbidities, is essential for maximizing life expectancy.

list.title: Past:
list.snippet: Before ART, HIV was a fatal illness, with a median survival time of 8-10 years.

list.title: Present:
list.snippet: With the advent of ART, life expectancy for people with HIV has dramatically increased and is now similar to the general population in many developed countries.

list.title: Future:
list.snippet: Continued advancements in ART, along with improved strategies for managing co-morbidities, are expected to further extend the lifespan of individuals living with HIV.
